title: DistributedMeanSquaredSmooth.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective is differentiable on all of ℝᵈ and may be nonconvex. It has a global lower bound a with f(x₀) − a ≤ Δ, where Δ ≥ 0. The infimum need not be attained.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Worker i takes a pair (x,y) and returns (gᵢ(x,ξ), gᵢ(y,ξ)) using the same fresh sample for both evaluations. Each estimate is unbiased for the gradient of the common objective. Samples are IID within a worker and streams are independent across workers. Each worker may have its own sampling law μᵢ.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanSquaredSmooth.lean, Query, system and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient.unbiased. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every worker i and point x, E‖gᵢ(x,ξ) − ∇f(x)‖² ≤ σ², with a common public σ ≥ 0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanSquaredSmooth.lean, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient.variance_integrable and IsStochasticGradient.variance.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The query points and output belong to ℝᵈ with its Euclidean norm. The dimension d is public.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params.d and Point. LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanSquaredSmooth.lean, Point, Query, spec.Output and spec.publicInput.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Each worker satisfies the same-sample mean-squared smoothness bound E‖gᵢ(x,ξ) − gᵢ(y,ξ)‖² ≤ L²‖x − y‖² for every x,y. The timed star has a noncomputing center and n ≥ 1 workers. A paired evaluation takes 2hᵢ time, with one pending computation per worker. Each directed center–worker link carries one message at a time. A k-bit payload takes l + b(k + 64) time, and distinct directed links and worker computations can operate concurrently. All parameters are public, including x₀, L > 0, Δ, σ, ε > 0, hᵢ > 0, l ≥ 0 and b ≥ 0. The objective, oracle maps and sampling laws are instance data.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanSquaredSmooth.lean, system, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, computation and communication. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, Time, clockBits and step.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns one measurable point X from its designated root's state at the prescribed elapsed-time deadline. The squared Euclidean gradient norm ‖∇f(X)‖² must be integrable.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanSquaredSmooth.lean, spec.Output and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute and TimedConvergence.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E‖∇f(X)‖² ≤ ε² under the product law of the algorithm seed and the oracle seed. The deadline is fixed by the public parameters, and execution must have finitely many events through that deadline almost surely.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanSquaredSmooth.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law, FiniteEvents and TimedConvergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The benchmark combines same-sample two-point stochastic gradients and per-worker mean-squared smoothness with a fixed elapsed-time guarantee on a star network. Worker speeds, concurrent directed links, message latency and individual transmitted bits all enter the cost model.

descriptionHtml:
Distributed Mean-Squared Smooth Nonconvex Optimization

We seek a stationary point of a differentiable, possibly nonconvex objective f:Rd→R in Euclidean dimension d≥0, given a starting point with bounded objective gap above a global lower bound. Workers on a star network have independent sample streams. Each completed query returns unbiased stochastic gradients at two points using one fresh sample. The gradients have bounded variance and are Lipschitz in mean square. Given ε>0, the goal is to return x¯∈Rd by an elapsed-time deadline with E∥∇f(x¯)∥2≤ε2, averaging over the samples and algorithm randomness.

The underlying optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). The algorithm receives the dimension d, the number of workers n≥1, the measurable sample space Ω, the starting point x0∈Rd, the bounds L>0, Δ≥0, and σ≥0, the tolerance ε, and the timing parameters (hi)i=1n, ℓ, and b described below. All norms are Euclidean.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Objective and initial gap). The function f is differentiable everywhere. There exists a∈R such that a≤f(x)for every x∈Rd,f(x0)−a≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Worker sampling). For each worker i∈{1,…,n}, the samples (ξi,k)k≥0 are measurable, independent, and identically distributed with law μi on Ω. The worker streams are mutually independent, and the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the full sample array. On its (k+1)st completed query, worker i returns, for any requested x,y∈Rd, the pair (gi(x,ξi,k),gi(y,ξi,k)).

Assumption 3 (Gradient moments and mean-squared smoothness). Each gi:Rd×Ω→Rd is jointly measurable. For every x,y∈Rd and ξ∼μi, the vector gi(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable, both squared norms below are integrable, and E[gi(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),E∥gi(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2≤σ2,E∥gi(x,ξ)−gi(y,ξ)∥2≤L2∥x−y∥2.

The star has one communication-only hub and n computing workers. A paired query at worker i takes 2hi units of time, where hi>0. Each worker can have one query in progress. It may abort that query without consuming a sample. Further evaluation requests while the worker is busy are ignored.

Messages travel between the hub and a worker in either direction. A payload of m≥0 bits is transmitted with 64 appended zero bits and takes ℓ+b(m+64) units of time, where ℓ≥0 is the latency and b≥0 is the time per transmitted bit. The recipient receives the sender’s identity and the transmitted bits. Each directed link carries at most one message at a time and ignores new submissions while occupied. Distinct directed links can operate concurrently, including opposite directions on the same edge. Computations at different workers can overlap with one another and with communication.

Let T≥0 be the elapsed-time budget. Almost surely, every deadline t∈[0,T] must be reached with only finitely many events. At time T, the algorithm’s designated output node must return a measurable point x¯ with integrable squared gradient norm satisfying E[∥∇f(x¯)∥2]≤ε2.

comparisonHtml:
The differentiable objective f:Rd→R satisfies f(x0)−inff≤Δ. Worker streams are independent, with IID samples of law μi within worker i. Its jointly measurable oracle satisfies Eμigi(x,ξ)=∇f(x), Eμi∥gi(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2≤σ2, and Eμi∥gi(x,ξ)−gi(y,ξ)∥2≤L2∥x−y∥2. On the coordinator star, worker i takes 2hi>0 per same-sample pair. A q-bit message takes ℓ+bq. Each worker handles one computation and each directed link one message at a time; distinct links and computations can overlap. The target is E∥∇f(X)∥2≤ε2 under the execution law, with almost surely finitely many events through the deadline.

import LongTails.Setups.DistributedSmoothNonconvex

open MeasureTheory DistributedTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistributedMeanSquaredSmooth

open StochasticSmoothAndConvex (IsStochasticGradient)
open StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex (IID)

abbrev Params := DistributedSmoothNonconvex.Params
abbrev Point := DistributedSmoothNonconvex.Point
abbrev Samples := DistributedSmoothNonconvex.Samples

abbrev Query (p : Params) := Point p × Point p
abbrev ComputeQuery (p : Params) := StarNetwork.ComputeQuery (Query p)
abbrev ComputeReply (p : Params) := StarNetwork.ComputeReply (Query p) (Query p)
abbrev CommReply (p : Params) := StarNetwork.CommReply p.n

noncomputable def system (p : Params) (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p)
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)) :
    Oracle (ComputeQuery p) (ComputeReply p) (CommReply p) (p.n + 1) :=
  StarNetwork.system ⟨fun i => 2 * p.h i, p.l, p.b⟩
    (fun i q s k => (g i q.1 (s i k), g i q.2 (s i k))) P

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  numWorkers p := p.n + 1
  Instance p := Point p → ℝ
  ComputeQuery := ComputeQuery
  ComputeReply := ComputeReply
  CommReply := CommReply
  Output := Point
  publicInput := id
  valid p := (∀ i, 0 < p.h i) ∧ 0 < p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.σ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∃ a : ℝ, (∀ x, a ≤ f x) ∧ f p.x0 - a ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ∃ (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p)
      (μ : Fin p.n → ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)),
      O = system p g P ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i (s : Samples p) => s i) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∀ i, IID (fun k (s : Samples p) => s i k) (μ i : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
        IsStochasticGradient (Point p) p.Ω (μ i) f (g i) p.σ ∧
        ∀ x y, Integrable (fun ξ => ‖g i x ξ - g i y ξ‖ ^ 2) (μ i : Measure _) ∧
          (∫ ξ, ‖g i x ξ - g i y ξ‖ ^ 2 ∂(μ i : Measure _)) ≤ p.L ^ 2 * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε ^ 2

end LongTails.Setups.DistributedMeanSquaredSmooth
